title: superset-new vs old superset vs upstream
window: superset-new 2026-10-20 21:54Z to 2026-10-21 02:31Z; old superset and upstream 2026-10-19/20

method.hardware: c8g.metal-24xl (96 Graviton4 cores), one server host and two or three client hosts per pod, same AZ and placement group, 0.10 ms client-server round trip
method.build: GCC 11.5, -O3 -flto, jemalloc, identical flags for all three builds
method.pinning: main thread core 1, IO thread i on core i+1, superset poller core 65, replication sender core 66, background threads 67-79, NIC IRQs 80-95, irqbalance off
method.client: memtier_benchmark 2.5.2 on cores 16-95 of each client host; 9,600 connections at P1, 2,304 at P16, 960 at P64
method.run: 3 reps per build, 10 s measurement window after warm-up; values are medians of the 3 reps. Only superset-new was run for this page; old superset and upstream are the earlier review's runs, same harness and connection counts
method.verdict: win/regress when the median ratio is beyond 5% and the two builds' rep ranges do not overlap, otherwise tie; high variance = CV over 5%
notes: io-threads equals write lanes in superset. io-threads 2 = main thread + 1 IO thread on both builds.
Superset's poller busy-waits on its own core from io-threads 8 up, so superset has one more core than upstream at the same io-threads value.
Superset IO threads and poller busy-poll, so they read ~100% CPU when idle; ops per CPU-second is comparable only at io-threads 8 or fewer.
NIC: a cell flagged N had the ENA allowance counters rise during the window; its numbers are lower bounds on server capacity.
Data types and the io-threads 8 half of tier 3 ran on a different server host with 2 client hosts for superset-new (3 before).
p100 includes connection setup; use p99.9.

regressions.title: 2 cores, pipelined
regressions.detail: 0.59-0.79x upstream on SET, 80/20, 50/50, HSET, HGET, SISMEMBER, XADD, XRANGE at P16/P64; same as old superset

regressions.title: ZADD (new in this build)
regressions.detail: 0.82-0.85x old superset at 1, 8 and 32 IO threads; 0.82x upstream at 1 IO thread

regressions.title: XADD
regressions.detail: 0.88-0.93x upstream at 8 and 32 IO threads; unchanged

regressions.title: Replica disconnect on SET-only
regressions.detail: replica link drops in every rep at 8, 16, 32 IO threads; peak lag 480-650 MB

regressions.title: Single thread
regressions.detail: 2-10% slower than upstream, worst SADD P16 0.90x
